lines: One lake holds 19% of unfrozen fresh water.
Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is also the world's oldest.
It formed 25 to 30 million years ago.
Its rift still widens about 4 millimetres a year.
Its basins reach 900, 1,600 and 1,400 metres deep.
Below 300 metres, it stays at 3.1 to 3.4 °C year-round.
Drain it, and a fifth of Earth's unfrozen fresh water disappears.
So one Siberian rift holds a startling share of our fresh water.
